version_note: This pack is mostly deterministic. On-chain facts are E4: verify by querying the chain, NOT by asking a model. The judgment layer only handles the residual semantic question (does the tx purpose match the claim), and only when the deterministic checks cannot fully settle it.
deterministic_precheck: tx hash exists on the declared chain (RPC query, L1) — MUST pass or hard reject
tx is confirmed (>= N confirmations, configurable)
from/to addresses match the declared wallet(s)
amount matches the claimed amount (exact arithmetic, code — never a model)
block height / timestamp within task window
wallet signature over challenge nonce is valid (identity binding)
skip_judgment_when: all deterministic checks pass AND the claim is a pure factual assertion about the transaction (amount, address, holding, block). In that case: verdict = approved deterministically, model_id = 'deterministic', judgment layer is NOT invoked. This is the near-zero-cost path.

state_template.claim: <claim, e.g. held >= 100 USDC at block X>

purpose_matches.instructions: The transaction facts are already verified deterministically (see state.l1_signals). Given the claim, does the PURPOSE of this transaction match what the task required (e.g. a payment for the right thing, to the right counterparty for this task), rather than an unrelated transfer that merely happens to satisfy the numbers?

posterior_rule.overall: 1.0 when judgment skipped (deterministic pass); else P(purpose_matches) gated by deterministic result
posterior_rule.note: If any deterministic check fails, hard reject in L1 — never let the model 'rescue' a transaction whose on-chain facts don't hold.
